minutes.headline: Fire chief pitched a fourth duty shift to end chronic forced overtime and thin ambulance staffing
minutes.summary: This was the first joint Select Board/School Committee/Finance Committee "tri-board" meeting, run by an outside facilitator, covering the fire department's proposed fourth shift, possible consolidation of town/school facilities, HR, legal and IT services, departmental growth pressures (special education, federal grant cuts), and financial-management controls after a revolving account ran into deficit. No consolidation, budget, or staffing item was put to a vote; the boards agreed to keep exploring facilities, HR and legal consolidation, to hold future tri-board meetings at Town Hall broadcast live, and to hold a dedicated public listening session in late October rather than public comment at every meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chief said forced-in Sunday shifts to cover paramedic staffing cost extra overtime in FY24 because Sunday coverage is paid at double time by contract.

budget_items.topic: Fire department fourth-shift proposal, total estimated cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The chief presented an educated-guess total cost for adding a fourth shift of three firefighter-paramedics, covering pay, overtime and holiday pay increases, and one new officer position.

budget_items.topic: Fire department fourth-shift proposal, new hires' base cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The cost of three new firefighter paramedics at step two was broken out separately from the overtime, holiday, uniform and OPEB cost components.

budget_items.topic: Fire department fourth-shift proposal, uniform allowance
budget_items.what_was_said: Each new hire's uniform allowance is set by contract per year, added to the fourth-shift cost estimate.
A school committee member said the district's guaranteed legal cost last year was a certain figure, used to argue for combining town and school legal services.
A board member cited the town's flat-rate contract figure for its lawyer from the prior year, contrasted with the school's hourly labor-attorney arrangement.

budget_items.topic: Trash/recycling cost and proposed enterprise fund
budget_items.what_was_said: A member cited what the town currently pays per year for recycling and proposed shifting trash/recycling to a self-funded enterprise fund, with savings potentially redirected to fund the fire department's fourth shift.
The finance director said the town saw a premium increase from its carrier this past year and has been told to expect at least the same increase again next year.
A school committee member described the cost range of out-of-district special education placements as a reason to invest in in-district BCBA staffing instead.

The superintendent said elimination of certain federal title grants for professional development and multilingual learner education has been reported statewide, which will affect the district's budget and the governor's earmark allowances.

A member described turning a parks and recreation department in a prior town of employment from a deficit to a profit over three years as an argument for making Lunenburg's recreation director full-time.

The finance director said one school revolving account went into a significant deficit this past school year because no budget had been entered for it in the town's financial system, so overspending wasn't flagged.

decisions.decision: The boards agreed facilities-department consolidation is worth exploring as a longer-term (FY26-FY28) possibility, not part of the current budget cycle.
The group narrowed its consolidation exploration list to facilities, HR, and legal/buying-power, while treating IT consolidation as a hard no per the school side.

Rather than a public comment period at every tri-board meeting, the group agreed to hold a dedicated public listening session around the end of October and to invite email/survey input at each meeting.
The finance director and a select board member agreed to draft a prioritized list of financial best practices to bring back to the committee.
The superintendent said hiring a business manager is the district's top financial-management priority right now.
The finance committee and superintendent agreed to aim for quarterly meetings going forward to avoid budget-season surprises.
The next tri-board meeting was set for August 26th per the already-circulated draft schedule.
Future tri-board meetings will be held at Town Hall, set up without using the stage, and broadcast live, rather than at the adult activity center.

what_happened.line: The fire chief proposed adding a fourth duty shift to end forced overtime and thin ambulance staffing, with no vote taken.
The three boards agreed to keep exploring consolidating town and school facilities, HR and legal services, but ruled out combining IT.
Rather than public comment at every joint meeting, the boards will hold a dedicated public listening session around the end of October.
The finance director said a school revolving account ran into a significant deficit last year because no budget had been entered for it, so overspending went unflagged.
The finance committee and superintendent agreed to start meeting quarterly, and the next tri-board session is set for August 26 at Town Hall, broadcast live.

why_it_matters: The fourth fire shift would change how ambulance and paramedic coverage is staffed and is an amount residents will eventually see reflected in a budget vote, not yet decided here.
